subject: Strategic SLA package and flexible pricing for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.io
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Acme is mapping out our vendor SLA needs for a Q3 rollout and we need a concise set of options we can present to procurement: uptime tiers, guaranteed response windows, escalation coverage, and indicative pricing (including any retainer for 24/7 critical support).

High-level context: we expect a steady baseline traffic (~1.5B tokens/mo) with spikes during product launches. Multi-region failover is a hard requirement.

Can you send a short menu with 2–3 package choices (recommended, high-availability, and premium with on-call) and any details on credits/penalties for downtime? Procurement will want a one-page summary first.

Appreciate it —
Michael
CTO, Acme Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the note and the context. I attached a concise SLA_Summary_v3.pdf with three packaged options and a short FAQ. Quick highlights:

- Recommended: 99.9% uptime, business-hours response (4 hr PRI, 1 business-day SEV triage), no retainer.
- High-availability: 99.95%, 24/7 monitoring + 4 hr response for SEV1, optional regional warm-standby (adds replication cost).
- Premium (enterprise): 99.99% SLO, 24/7 on-call retainer with guaranteed 1-hour response and an assigned escalation manager. Includes runbook walkthroughs and quarterly DR exercises.

Before we finalize numbers, can you confirm: (1) target committed spend or term length you expect to commit to (12/24 months), and (2) which regions are required for failover? I’ll loop in Aditya on pricing ranges so we can show a clean menu for procurement.

Attachment: SLA_Summary_v3.pdf (pdf, 198 KB)

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.io, Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@acme.io>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Soojin —

Thanks for the summary. A couple of clarifying points before Procurement will review:

- Estimated peak: we can hit ~5–6B tokens during launches for short windows; baseline remains ~1.5B/mo.
- Failover: primary US + secondary EU required, APAC optional but preferred.
- Credits: procurement will want a clear credit matrix for availability bands and a description of how regional failover counts toward uptime calculations.
- On-call: for the premium option we’re trying to understand the retainer model (flat monthly vs hours consumed) and whether the retainer buys guaranteed engineer allocation or faster rotation queueing.

Can you provide an indicative price band for both 12- and 24-month commitments?

Michael

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Michael, Soojin —

Following up with indicative pricing bands (ballpark; final quote subject to committed capacity):

- Recommended (99.9%): $0.08–$0.11 per 1k tokens at baseline volumes (volume tiers reduce unit price). No retainer. 12mo/24mo commit: 5–12% discount.
- High-availability (99.95%): +15–25% on unit price vs recommended (adds replication & warm standby). 12mo commit ~10% discount, 24mo ~15%.
- Premium (99.99% + 1-hour SEV1): retainer options — $12k/mo flat retainer for guaranteed 2-hour engineer SLA (up to X incidents), or $20k/mo retainer for dedicated rotation (on-call engineer assigned to account). Retainer can be offset against committed usage (credit applied monthly).

Credit matrix (draft): availability band <99.9% => 10% credit; <99.5% => 25% credit; <99.0% => case-by-case higher credit + dedicated investigation (refunds calculated on monthly invoice). We’ll formalize language for contract.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (xlsx, 84 KB)

Aditya
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Michael —

Thanks for the details. To make procurement’s life easier we propose a "Flex Ladder" approach: a two-phase commercial that lowers initial commitment friction and increases coverage as you ramp. Proposed structure: 

Phase 1 (Pilot — 30 days):
- 99.9% baseline SLA, no retainer, capped pilot spend for proofs.
- Transparent playbook for failover tests (we’ll run a joint tabletop).

Phase 2 (Commit — production): pick one of the packaged levels with the following commercial levers:
- 12-month commit = base unit price minus 10%
- 24-month commit = base unit price minus 16%
- Retainer discount: if you add a 12mo retainer (enterprise on-call) we can discount retainer by 15%; for a 24mo retainer we can go to 25% off the retainer.

Additional notes: regional failover is measured at the application layer; if warm-standby is enabled across regions we count failover events for credit only if both regions show degraded performance per the runbook.

Next steps: if that structure is acceptable, we’ll produce a one-page commercial summary and a draft SOW for procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.io, Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@acme.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Marissa, Soojin —

The Flex Ladder looks promising. A few counter-points from procurement: 

- Retainer level: $20k/mo (dedicated rotation) is on the high side for our initial term. Would you consider $14k/mo for a 12-month committed retainer (we can revisit at renewal)?
- Credits: procurement wants the credit matrix tightened with explicit time-to-resolution targets tied to credits (e.g., SEV1 not resolved within 1 hour => X% credit).
- DocuSign path: we prefer a single DocuSign flow that ties the SOW, pricing appendix, and retainer terms.

If you can meet $14k/mo retainer for 12mo and provide the tightened credit triggers we’ll move to sign.

Thanks —
Michael
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Michael Reyes <michael.reyes@acme.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options & pricing — initial ask

Michael —

Appreciate the candid counter. Quick response: we can accept a concession to accelerate the deal:

- Retainer: agree to $14k/mo for a 12-month dedicated rotation with the following caveat: we’ll include a 30-day early-evaluation clause where either party can request an operational review; after month 3 we’ll commit to a joint SLA health check and potentially expand coverage.
- Credits: we’ll tighten the credit triggers and include explicit TTR (time-to-repair) buckets tied to credit percentages in the appendix (SEV1 >1hr => 10% credit; SEV1 >4hr => 25% credit; additional terms for regional failover events included).
- DocuSign: I’m attaching a DocuSign link for the commercial summary + SOW + retainer appendix. Please have your procurement team review and I’ll set a follow-up to confirm signatures.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-SLA-v3

If that sounds good I can route a final one-page commercial summary to procurement today.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_Summary_v3.pdf (updated)
